# NOTES ON THE TEXT (two books)

## BOOK 1: "Pride and His Prisoners" by A. L. O. E. (Gutenberg 60149)

**Frame/Prologue (Ch. I-III):** Nettleby Tower, Somersetshire, ruined Norman tower on hill, owned by Mr. Auger (who won lawsuit); Dr. Timon Bardon disinherited by proud father (Hugh Bardon) for marrying a farmer's daughter. Tower said to be haunted by spirits Pride (tall, deep voice, bat-like wing) and Intemperance (wild red-meteor eyes). Dialogue: Pride boasts of influence on Hugh Bardon; Intemperance boasts of gin-palaces. Pride's three fermentations (vinous, acid, last stage). Pride's footnote: pastor's quip "The devil told me the same thing." Pride targets Ida Aumerle (pastor's daughter, soft dark eyes; "Ithuriel's spear"). Pride's arts: "pardonable weakness," "natural instinct," "generous virtue." Ch. III: Pride watches Vicar Lawrence Aumerle's wife's death; Augustine Aumerle (younger brother, handsome, sceptic, Cambridge honours, reads German philosophy); Timon Bardon with long white hair. Author's note: reader should ask whether he is a prisoner of Pride.

**Ch. II:** Ida at 12 lost mother; sister Mabel (younger, impulsive, fearless, upturned nose). Ida's conversion at age ~16-17 (Bible reading, tears). Ida at 18 at uncle Augustine's home Aspendale; suitor Reginald, Earl of Dashleigh (Augustine's college friend); Ida refused him; he then proposed to cousin Annabella (Ida's cousin, daughter of mother's sister). Ida's father Lawrence remarries Miss Lambert (Mrs. Aumerle, practical, stepmother; "Barbara Aumerle"). Pride stirs step-daughters' resentment; Ida dethroned; Mrs. Aumerle vetoes Ida's choir trio and Ida's farm-boys class (Ida wanted it on Saturday evening; Mrs. Aumerle proposes to take lads herself and give Ida the mothers' meeting). Ida has "Pride of self-will."

**Ch. IV:** Cottage of Dr. Bardon (Mill Cottage, "Milton Cottage" per Cecilia's affectation). Cecilia Bardon (30-40, sallow, vain of dress, fawn kid boots, pink cards of countess's wedding). Dr. Bardon (leonine, long white hair, "sick of cards", says "It's the fool that gets on in the world"). Ida and Mabel bring crimson curtain. Annabella's invitation to Dashleigh Hall. Bardon's pride; Venice Sumach.

**Ch. V:** Mabel's "porcelain vs crockery"; Mabel's "mental glass" joke about Bardon. Mrs. Aumerle's scolding about walking after sunset; Ida-Mrs.Aumerle dispute on the class.

**Ch. VI:** Visit to Dashleigh Hall in a donkey-chaise hired from farmer; Cecilia's dusty flounces; Bardon's "gingerbread"; countess greets them warmly; Annabella's flower-bed and slip of Venice Sumach wins Bardon.

**Ch. VII:** Annabella's background (orphan, grandmother; pen-name "Egeria"; love/ambition). Earl's pride and pique; marriage sours; Pride whispers to each. Earl's fall from horse at donkey's bray; Earl (Dashleigh) orders Bardons turned away; Annabella asked to dismiss them. Bardon's outburst "Can't you manage ... these miserable Bardons?" overheard; Bardon denounces Earl; Annabella weeps.

**Ch. VIII:** Vicar Lawrence and Augustine argue (German philosophy; Psalm 131; "Reason ... handmaid"; origin of sin; "You do not know your own weakness and sin"). Augustine stalks off; Lawrence prays.

**Ch. IX:** Annabella's romance "Egeria" proofs; earl forbids publication/payment; "tyrant" (Pride). Annabella writes satirical "The Precipice and the Peer" (Swiss mountain episode; boa).

**Ch. X:** Mabel and Ida in arbour: "ladder of good works," "golden cord," "dearest idol" hymn. Pride baffled.

**Ch. XI:** Earl learns from Augustine Verdon the aeronaut's balloon *Eaglet* trial at Aspendale; Annabella taunts earl; earl tears her manuscript (discovered by Duke of Montleroy); earl orders her out; Annabella sends maid Bates, decides to go to vicarage. Servants gossip.

**Ch. XII:** Evening at vicarage; Cecilia sings "Bel raggio"; Mabel asks to go in balloon; Mrs. Aumerle: "That's pride"; Bardon refuses to meet Dashleigh; Annabella arrives in storm; Ida takes her to study.

**Ch. XIII:** Mrs. Aumerle vs Mabel; Augustine's mission to earl (earl consents to pardon if she asks and returns). Annabella refuses: "I will not go and beg pardon." Calls Bardon.

**Ch. XIV:** Bardon advises publishing "Precipice" in revenge; sends countess to publish. Annabella sends manuscript to magazine editor and letter to publisher (to put "Countess of Dashleigh" on title). Ida tries to speak, is refused. Annabella hesitates at window when Mabel offers to call Bates back; "too late."

**Ch. XV:** Earl sees magazine advertisement; reads "The Precipice and the Peer." Vicar's letter to earl. Earl plans balloon ascent to prove courage; writes note to Augustine.

**Ch. XVI:** Ida pleads with Annabella; Mrs. Aumerle rebukes Ida; Annabella leaves to Mill Cottage with Bates. Ida regrets not pleading earlier.

**Ch. XVII:** Bardon buys magazine in Pelton; gloats; walks six miles. Bardon's Christianity; Lord's Prayer irony. Librarian reports "a hit."

**Ch. XVIII:** Bardon reads magazine at Mrs. Clayton's (blind widow); "cochlico lozenges"; learns Mr. Auger died (of Nettleby Tower). Annabella lodges at Mill Cottage; Cecilia's sacrifices; Bates disdains cottage.

**Ch. XIX:** Earl to ascend in *Eaglet*; Mabel gets father's "opinion" permission; Mrs. Aumerle refuses; vicar agrees with wife.

**Ch. XX:** Morning of 12th May; Mabel drives with Augustine on Black Prince; Aspendale Lodge; Verdon ("small man, keen grey eyes"); Bardon taunts ("lion and bear"); earl arrives pale.

**Ch. XXI:** Earl panics; wine; grabs "Let go!"; balloon launched prematurely; Verdon: "Merciful Heaven! they are lost!" Bardon rides off.

**Ch. XXII:** Ascent; Augustine pulls valve rope, it snaps; cloud; whirlwind; earl senseless.

**Ch. XXIII:** Ida confesses to Mrs. Aumerle; Bardon rides to vicarage: "Lost!" Annabella curses him; "never enter my presence."

**Ch. XXIV:** Night aloft; earl's repentance ("Death is a great preacher"); Mabel's letter dropped; earl drops pocket-book with Annabella's gift (two words written in it); prayer (Litany).

**Ch. XXV:** Ida's penitence; Mrs. Aumerle embraces Ida; "faults on both sides."

**Ch. XXVI:** Augustine's prayer/reflection at dawn; balloon descends into sea; ballast cast; car sinks; Augustine cuts ropes; rescue by fishing smack/sail.

**Ch. XXVII:** Telegram from Augustine ("Safe, thank God!... Cliff Cottage, B——, Devon... brain fever"); Annabella cancels her romance's publication; Mrs. Aumerle's letter-opening; Mabel's letter reached home.

**Ch. XXVIII:** Bardon inherits Nettleby Tower by Auger's will. Travellers reach Devon by night; fisherman's cottage.

**Ch. XXIX:** Dr. G—— forbids Annabella's entry; earl's pocket-book returned with "forgiveness" and "peace" written in pencil; reconciliation.

**Ch. XXX:** July; earl recovered; visits Bardon at Nettleby Tower; handshake; epilogue on Pride with poem.

Key characters Book 1: Dr. Timon Bardon; Cecilia Bardon; Vicar Lawrence Aumerle; Mrs. Barbara Aumerle; Ida; Mabel; Augustine Aumerle; Annabella (Countess of Dashleigh); Reginald, Earl of Dashleigh; Bates (maid); Duke of Montleroy; Mr. Verdon (aeronaut); Mrs. Clayton; Mrs. Graham; Black Prince (horse); balloon *Eaglet*; Mr. Auger (dead); Dr. G——; Pride, Intemperance (spirits); Mrs. Aumerle's "Mullins" (coachman).

## BOOK 2: "The Clock Struck One" by Fergus Hume (Gutenberg 55689)

**Ch. I:** Dora Carew (tall, grey-eyed, bicycle, "Diana on a bicycle") meets Dr. Allen Scott (lover) on road two miles from Canterbury; Dr. Scott's new patient Lady Burville (Laura Burville) at Hernwood Hall, guest of Sir Harry Hernwood, with Mr. Pallant. Dora's guardian Julian Edermont (Red House, Chillum) fainted during Litany prayer ("From battle and murder, and from sudden death, good Lord, deliver us") when Lady Burville appeared in Chillum Church. Gate locked; postern locked.

**Ch. II:** Lambert Joad (drunk, lecherous, ex-parson, Edermont's college friend, sleeps in cottage across road; leaves at 9 pm). Joad: "So like your father" — knew Allen's father (Dr. Scott, d. when Allen was 5). Joad: "ask Lady Burville." Edermont calls from window: "Do not talk of that woman." Allen flees.

**Ch. III:** Edermont terrified, says "Allen Scott will never marry you"; reveals nothing but "your parents sinned." Dora threatens; Edermont warns against Lady Burville. Joad at gate ("you will never marry Allen"). Canterbury trip.

**Ch. IV:** Mrs. Tice (Allen's nurse/housekeeper, Canterbury, green-doored house). Allen gone to London (Selling station, 4:26 train). Mrs. Tice recognises Edermont's photo (a young man); knows secret; "you will never become the wife of Allen Scott."

**Ch. V:** Week passes; Edermont cheerful; Allen silent; house locked nightly; Edermont fears robbers. Pallant's visit (Edermont says "nightmare at an end"; faints).

**Ch. VI:** Pallant: "Beware of Allen Scott!" Allen writes he'll return Aug 2. Edermont writes letters (to Allen, others). Aug 2 night: Edermont and Dora's talk (toothache). Clock strikes one. Cry in night; Dora sleeps. Dawn: Meg Gance (cook) finds Edermont dead, head bashed.

**Ch. VII:** Study scene: bureau smashed; knobkerrie (Zulu club); pistol. Joad arrives early through drawing-room glass door (open); postern open. Inspector Jedd. Allen returns; Dora breaks; Allen breaks off engagement, cites secret.

**Ch. VIII:** Inquest (witnesses Meg, Dora, Joad, Dr. Chambers—death between 12-1, Jedd). Will: fifty thousand pounds to whoever punishes assassin; Dora gets Red House + £200/yr on condition Joad stays. Manuscript "story of my life" in bureau sealed.

**Ch. IX:** Morning Planet article on reward. Dora learns no £500/yr; Carver (lawyer, Mercery Lane) says Edermont lied; "a woman at the bottom of everything."

**Ch. X:** Dora visits Allen; Allen refuses secret; Mrs. Tice to stay at Red House.

**Ch. XI:** Mrs. Tice admits she knew Edermont at Christchurch (nurse for Dr. and Mrs. Scott). Dora deduces Christchurch link; tries Joad's admiration.

**Ch. XII:** Joad drunk, falls in love; Dora learns Joad knew Edermont's secret; Joad reveals: Allen was at Red House night of 2 Aug; accuses Allen; demands Dora marry him in a week or he denounces.

**Ch. XIII:** Denial; Joad's account (he saw Allen on bicycle at midnight, Pride arrived ~midnight; Joad alibi with Pride till 2). Dora rides to Allen.

**Ch. XIV:** Allen confesses presence; shows Edermont's midnight letter; saw body dead; panicked; met a woman on bicycle (Lady Burville) near Chillum/railway bridge; repaired her tyre; Allen found brooch in study.

**Ch. XV:** Pearl brooch "L.B." Dora gets Lady Burville's address (22 Jersey Place, Mayfair) from Sir Harry Hernwood (fool). Dora tells Mrs. Tice she is going to London.

**Ch. XVI:** Dora on train meets Pride (protégé; Edermont's; plump, rosy, white beard). Pride admits being with Joad at one; met a man and woman on bicycles. At Lady Burville's (Mayfair mansion; portrait of Sir John Burville): Lady Burville: "I am your mother!"

**Ch. XVII:** Lady Burville's story: real name Laura Treherne; first husband Captain George Theophilus Carew (sea captain, ship *Silver Arrow*); Julian Dargill (rich, Edermont's real name) married her after Carew "died"; Dora born; Carew returned; Dargill fled; annuity; Lady Burville married Sir John Burville; Pallant blackmailer from America. Lady Burville says Carew killed Dargill.

**Ch. XVIII:** Dora promises silence. Pallant visits: Carew died in San Francisco (Pallant with him); Pallant blackmailed Lady Burville; Edermont "dead" = Carew dead. Mrs. Tice: Allen ill (letter from servant Emma). Dora tells Mrs. Tice she's Lady Burville's daughter.

**Ch. XIX:** Dora: father Carew dead, glad. Pallant denies being killer; says burglary; "your clock might have been wrong" (Pallant's remark). Mrs. Tice's story (Christchurch): Carew shot Dr. Scott (Allen's father) by mistake at drawing-room window. Mrs. Tice's version: Carew shot Dr. Scott; Dora learns Allen can't marry daughter of his father's murderer.

**Ch. XX:** Allen ill in sofa; Dora resolves to marry Joad to save Allen. Allen reveals he went to London, learned in *Morning Planet* file the murder; Edermont told him Dora was daughter of murderer. Dora reveals Lady Burville is her mother.

**Ch. XXI:** Allen reconstructs: Edermont's letters to Lady Burville re packet of letters; Pallant. Dora decides Pallant not killer.

**Ch. XXII:** Dora's clock deduction: Meg says hall clock an hour fast morning after (struck thirteen-like hint). Dora searches Joad's cottage (key under water-butt), finds manuscript "The Confession of Julian Dargill" in fireplace ashes.

**Ch. XXIII:** Joad confronts Dora: "Lost!" Dora reads manuscript begins; hides in wardrobe. Joad goes to Canterbury to see Carver. Dora to Carver: Carver to arrest Joad.

**Ch. XXIV:** Allen and Dora read manuscript: Julian Dargill born Christchurch; Laura Treherne; Carew; Dargill's second marriage; Dora is his daughter; Carew killed Dr. Scott (not Dargill) at drawing-room window; Dargill hid as Edermont; John Mallison (Dargill's friend) assumed name, fled to America; Dargill bought Red House.

**Ch. XXV:** Mrs. Tice told Dora's parentage; Allen: "bar removed." Carver arrives: Joad confessed (not murderer, accessory). Carver: Joad knew via letter (Edermont's letter to Lady Burville), altered clock, hid; Lady Burville came, Edermont showed manuscript; Mallison (= Pride) came in, fight, Edermont killed by Mallison's knobkerrie.

**Ch. XXVI:** Joad dies of heart disease on doorstep night arrest of Mallison/Pride (arrested in Joad's cottage). Lady Burville confesses to Sir John; Sir John re-marries her; Pallant shot in San Francisco gambling shop. Mallison (Pride) condemned and confesses (killed in self-defence; wanted manuscript). Final: Joad's will leaves £50,000 to Dora; Dora marries Allen in spring; Carver's surprise. "THE END."

**Key characters Book 2:** Dora Carew (Dargill); Dr. Allen Scott; Julian Edermont/Julian Dargill (victim); Lambert Joad (accomplice/accessory); Lady Burville/Laura (Treherne, Carew, Dargill, Burville); Captain George Theophilus Carew (father, d. San Francisco); Augustus Pallant (blackmailer); John Mallison/Mr. Pride (killer); Meg Gance (cook); Mrs. Tice (housekeeper, Scott nurse); Carver (lawyer); Inspector Jedd; Sir Harry Hernwood; Sir John Burville; Dr. Chambers; Dr. Scott (Allen's father, killed by Carew, d. ~20 years earlier); Emma (servant); Mrs. Clayton (not in Book 2); Red House; Chillum; Canterbury; Hernwood Hall; Jersey Place Mayfair; the Morning Planet; the hall clock (set an hour fast by Joad).
